2026 and 2027 exam windows: what is still open

As of early October 2026, the application deadline for the last API 936 window of 2026 has passed, so the next realistic 936 sitting is April 2027. The next open API 653 window is March to April 2027, with applications due in early January. API runs each certification in fixed three-week testing windows, with application deadlines roughly two months before each window opens.

Source: API Individual Certification Programs, Schedules and Fees page, read 4 October 2026. Confirm dates there before you apply; API occasionally adjusts windows. Two practical points follow from the calendar. First, 936 and 653 never share a window, so a crew lead can stagger candidates without double-booking study time. Second, each window has its own publication effectivity sheet. Study the editions listed for the window you book, not the editions in a borrowed binder.

Delivery also differs. API states that the 936 exam can be taken at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring, which matters to field hands who rotate between sites. API 653 is delivered in person at designated Prometric test centres only, so candidates need to plan travel to a centre around the window.

The refractory ladder: API 936 to API 982 Refractory Inspector

API now has a second refractory credential above 936. API 982 Refractory Inspector requires an active API 936 certification held for at least three years, plus general refractory experience with an inspection or supervision component that depends on education. That gives 936 holders a defined next step that does not depend on moving into tanks, vessels or piping.

Earlier versions of this question treated API 936 as a single, narrow card. That is no longer the whole picture. According to API's 982 program page, the Refractory Inspector certification covers the inspection and assessment of refractory linings, including material properties, defect mechanisms, in-service inspection methods, quality control, repair techniques and documentation. Where 936 is centred on installation quality control, 982 moves into evaluating linings in service: hot spots, spalling, erosion, cracking and repair decisions during turnarounds.

Education (per API's 982 page)General refractory experienceOf which inspection or supervision
Bachelor's in engineering or technology, or 3+ years technical military service3 years1 year

In every case the candidate must also hold an active API 936 for at least three years. The 982 exam, per API, is 4.5 hours with 165 questions (150 scored), closed book with no reference material, at a test centre or by remote proctoring. It runs in the same windows as 936. The certification term is three years, with work requirements, 8 CPD hours per cycle and a web quiz every six years.

For a welder, the realistic timeline looks like this: sit 936 in 2027, work refractory turnarounds and log the inspection and supervision portion carefully, and become eligible for 982 no earlier than 2030. That is a credible specialist career on its own, and it runs in parallel with, not instead of, the API 653 route described above. The two ladders reward different temperaments. Refractory work is concentrated in shutdown windows on FCC units, sulfur plants, reformers, heaters and boilers. Tank inspection is steadier, terminal and refinery-based, and carries signature authority under API 653.

Recertification and keeping each card alive

Both certifications run three-year terms, but keeping API 653 requires continued tank inspection work and CPD hours, while keeping API 936 is lighter. A person who takes 936 and then moves into tank inspection will be keeping two cards with different upkeep.

  • API 936: three-year term; API's page describes an online open-book quiz every six years, with a renewal application window opening 90 days before expiry and a 90-day grace period.
  • API 653: three-year term; API requires at least 20% of working time over the most recent three-year period on tank inspection activities, 24 continuing professional development hours per cycle, and a 25-question web quiz every six years with a four-hour limit.
  • API 982: three-year term; work requirement, 8 CPD hours per cycle and a web quiz every six years.

The 20% work requirement is the one that catches people. An API 653 holder who drifts back to welding or to refractory turnarounds for three years may not meet it at renewal. If you plan to hold both 936 and 653, keep the same kind of contemporaneous activity log for recertification that you kept for initial eligibility.

How big each community is

API's own ICP statistics presentation, dated April 2024, listed 2,616 active API 936 certifications and 9,885 active API 653 certifications. The refractory community is roughly a quarter the size of the tank inspector community. That is useful context for anyone weighing which card to chase.

A smaller credential pool cuts both ways. During a large turnaround, refractory QC roles can be hard to fill, and a 936 card makes a candidate immediately useful to refractory contractors and third-party surveillance firms. Outside turnaround season there are fewer full-time positions than in tank inspection, and the work follows the shutdown calendar. API 653 holders are more numerous but also tied to a much larger asset base: every terminal, refinery tank farm and many chemical, fertilizer and power plant tanks need periodic API 653 inspection. Neither number is a promise of jobs in any particular region; treat them as the scale of each community, not a forecast.

Upskilling a construction-side crew: a planning model

For a crew that has mostly worked on the construction side, the practical plan is to split people by role. Put the detail-oriented, documentation-minded people into API 936 for refractory QC work. Move one or two others into NDT technician roles inside an authorized inspection agency so their time counts toward API 653. Review each person's documented inspection time once a year against API's eligibility table. If you want help structuring the NDT side, ask us for a crew qualification plan.

The constraint that shapes the plan is the one already covered above: API states that API 653 experience must have been acquired within the last 10 years while employed by, or under contract with, an authorized inspection agency as API 653 defines it. A construction contractor's crew cannot create that experience on its own payroll. The options are to place people with an inspection company or owner inspection organization, or to set up a contractual arrangement in which the crew works under the direction of an owner-operator's inspection program. The second option is a business decision for the company and its clients; check the API 653 definitions against your actual contracts before counting on it.

A workable year-by-year model:

  1. Months 0 to 6: select candidates; register 936 candidates for the April 2027 window; start ASNT SNT-TC-1A qualification in visual testing and ultrasonic thickness testing for the people heading toward tank inspection, under a written practice that a Level III maintains.
  2. Months 6 to 18: 936 holders work refractory turnarounds as QC personnel; NDT technicians work tank jobs inside an authorized inspection agency, logging dates, tank IDs, activities performed and supervising inspector for each job.
  3. Months 18 to 24: NDT technicians who have a documented year of inspection performance and the general experience their education tier requires apply for API 653; 936 holders keep logging toward the three-year 982 threshold.

Keep the logs independent of any one employer's filing system. API verifies the experience claimed on the application after it is submitted, and a contemporaneous record with supervisor names is far easier to verify than a reconstruction.

FCC regenerator dryout: what to expect in the contractor's documentation

A common question from 936 holders on their first FCC job is what a complete dryout and acceptance package should contain. In outline: material and applicator qualification records, installation and sampling records, test results for samples taken during installation, a planned dryout curve with ramp rates and holds, the recorded thermocouple data against that plan, and documented acceptance at each hold point the owner's specification defines.

API Standard 936 is now in its fifth edition (2024, according to standards catalogue listings); the existing guide above describes the fourth edition of 2014. Its subject is installation quality control of monolithic refractory linings, and it is written to supplement the owner's specification. That division matters when you review dryout documentation. The heat-up schedule is normally set by the refractory manufacturer and the owner's engineer for the specific materials and lining thickness. The 936-qualified inspector's job is to verify that what happened in the field matches what was specified and to record deviations.

Items reviewers typically check on an FCC regenerator lining package:

  • Material traceability: product data sheets, batch or lot numbers, shelf-life and storage conditions for the castable or gunning mix actually installed.
  • Applicator and equipment qualification: evidence that each gunning or casting crew and its equipment were qualified on test panels before production, with results.
  • Anchor installation: anchor type, spacing and weld checks against the drawing, typically verified before refractory placement.
  • Installation records: water addition, mixing time, ambient and material temperature, and sample collection at the frequency the specification sets.
  • Sample test results: laboratory results on samples taken during installation, compared with specified acceptance values.
  • Visual and soundness inspection: post-installation checks of the lining, with any repairs mapped and requalified.
  • Dryout: the approved dryout curve, thermocouple locations, the recorded temperature trace, any interruptions or excursions and their disposition, and sign-off at each hold point.

Specific acceptance values and test frequencies come from the owner's specification and the current edition of API Standard 936. Check them against a licensed copy. Do not take numbers from training notes or forum posts. Crews that also need NDT qualification for turnaround work can request NDT training for refractory and turnaround crews.

Jurisdiction notes for the US and Canada

API certifications are private credentials, not government licences. In the United States, the requirement to use an API 653 inspector usually comes through the owner's program and, for oil storage, the EPA's Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure rule, which requires each aboveground container to be tested or inspected for integrity on a regular schedule and after material repairs. Industry standards such as API 653 (see how API 653 sets tank inspection intervals) and STI SP001 are the usual way owners meet that requirement. Refractory QC has no comparable federal certification requirement; owners set it in their specifications and contracts.

In Canada, provincial regulators control who may inspect regulated pressure equipment; for example, Alberta's ABSA runs its own inspector certification and owner-user program framework. Atmospheric storage tanks are generally handled differently from pressure equipment and vary by province and product. A welder planning to work in Canada should confirm with the provincial authority and with prospective employers which credentials they recognise, and should not assume an API card alone is sufficient.

More questions welders and crew leads ask

When is the API 936 exam in 2026?

API's 2026 windows for 936 were 10 April to 1 May, 7 to 28 August, and 4 to 25 December. The December application deadline was 2 October 2026, so new applicants should plan for 9 to 30 April 2027, with applications due 4 February 2027.

Can I take the API 936 exam remotely?

Yes. API states 936 can be scheduled at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring. API 653 is in person at Prometric test centres only.

What is the difference between API 936 and API 982?

API 936 Refractory Personnel centres on installation quality control of monolithic linings and has no experience prerequisite. API 982 Refractory Inspector covers inspection and assessment of linings, including in-service inspection and repair, and requires an active 936 held at least three years plus refractory and inspection experience.

Is API 936 a refractory inspector certification?

It is commonly called that, but API's title is Refractory Personnel. API's credential titled Refractory Inspector is API 982, which builds on 936.

Does API 936 time count toward API 982?

Holding 936 for three years is a prerequisite for 982, and refractory work done as a 936 holder can count toward the general refractory and inspection experience API requires. Document the inspection and supervision portion separately.

How many people hold API 936 compared with API 653?

API's April 2024 ICP statistics listed 2,616 active API 936 and 9,885 active API 653 certifications.

What does a contractor's dryout documentation for an FCC regenerator need to show?

The approved dryout curve, thermocouple layout, the recorded temperature trace against the plan, deviations and their disposition, and hold-point sign-offs, alongside material, applicator, installation and sample-test records. Acceptance values come from the owner's specification and the current API Standard 936.

How does Atlantis help a crew make this move?

Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training (see NDT Level II training and how ASNT certification works), online, live-virtual or onsite at your facility, with ASNT Level III oversight; our trainers have taught 1,000+ technicians. We do not provide API 936, 982 or 653 exam preparation. For tank owners, Atlantis performs tank NDE and delivers results to the owner's API 653 inspector, who stays inspector of record.
